summary: Recurring/mandate path is genuinely enabled and wired at every layer. Razorpay test mode settles token debits asynchronously: /payments/create/recurring returns only razorpay_payment_id (no status) and the bank authenticates/captures minutes later. This caused historical 'payment_pending' sessions; the merchant now parses the payment id, auto-reconciles pending sessions in the background, and the dashboard converges with Razorpay without operator action. Verified end-to-end with a fresh headless order that self-completed.

order_mandate_block.note: method=card + token{max_amount,expire_at,frequency} present on live authorization-transaction order

zero_ui_auto_charge_proof.audit_summary: Charging saved Visa 4366 server-side via token
zero_ui_auto_charge_proof.note: zero-UI recurring charge reached the gateway; the payment created first ('yet to be authenticated by the bank') and was captured asynchronously by the test sandbox.

async_settlement_and_auto_reconcile.root_cause: create/recurring returns razorpay_payment_id WITHOUT a status field; code read body.status -> None -> 'Gateway state None unresolved'. Payment sits created at the bank and captures minutes later; single-shot reconcile read the order list too early.
fixes: charge_with_token parses razorpay_payment_id and parks pending with the real payment id
reconcile_pending enriches by payment.fetch(id) and maps captured/authorized/failed/created
background reconcile worker (merchant lifespan) polls every ~30s and finalises captured sessions; boot pass adopts already-pending sessions
transient customer-setup errors (RemoteDisconnected) retried idempotently and never permanently decline a checkout
